Abyssinian: an Abyssinian is identified by its short, ticked coat with bands of color on each hair, large alert ears, a wedge-shaped head, and a slender, muscular body with a graceful, active posture.
american bulldog: an american bulldog is identified by a muscular, stocky build with a broad, square-shaped head, pronounced jaw muscles, short smooth coat often in white with patches of brindle, brown, or black, and ears that are medium-sized, folded forward, and set high.
american pit bull terrier: an american pit bull terrier is identified by a muscular, compact build with a broad, wedge-shaped head, pronounced jaw muscles, short glossy coat, and ears that are either cropped or naturally medium-sized and folded.
basset hound: a basset hound is identified by extremely long, droopy ears that reach past the nose, a deeply wrinkled forehead and loose skin around the face and neck, short crooked legs with heavy bone structure, and a low-slung, elongated body with a prominent.
beagle: a beagle is identified by its short, tri-color coat (typically white with black and tan patches), large floppy ears that reach past the nose, a compact muscular build, and a distinctive hound-like facial expression with soulful, wide-set brown eyes and slightly wrinkled.
Bengal: a Bengal is identified by its distinctive leopard-like spotted or marbled coat pattern with high-contrast, well-defined rosettes or arrowhead markings, often accompanied by a shimmering, iridescent “glitter” effect on the fur and a muscular, athletic build.
Birman: a Birman is identified by its pointed coat pattern with creamy body and dark brown or seal-colored points, white “gloves” on all four paws extending symmetrically up the front legs, and deep blue eyes.
Bombay: a Bombay is identified by its sleek, jet-black coat with a coppery sheen, large rounded eyes that are vivid copper or gold, and a muscular, compact body with a short, glossy fur and a distinctly rounded head with prominent cheeks.
boxer: a boxer is identified by a short, smooth coat with brindle, fawn, or white coloration; a square, muscular build; a distinctive pushed-in nose; and pronounced facial wrinkles, especially around the muzzle.
British Shorthair: a British Shorthair is identified by its dense, plush coat with a distinctive “crisp” texture, rounded face with full cheeks, large round copper or gold eyes, and stocky, muscular build with short, thick legs.
chihuahua: a chihuahua is identified by its apple-shaped skull with a prominent domed forehead, large erect ears relative to head size, short fine coat (or long silky coat with feathering), and disproportionately large eyes set wide apart.
Egyptian Mau: an Egyptian Mau is identified by its naturally spotted coat with random, dark, contrasting spots on a silver, bronze, or smoke background; a distinctive “M” marking on the forehead; large, alert, gooseberry-green eyes; and a muscular, medium-sized body with.
english cocker spaniel: an English cocker spaniel is identified by its rounded skull, short square muzzle, low-set long silky ears with feathering, expressive dark eyes, and a compact, sturdy body with abundant wavy or flat coat—often in solid colors or parti-color patterns with distinct facial.
english setter: an English setter is identified by its long, silky, feathered coat with distinctive white base color and speckled or mottled chestnut, lemon, orange, or liver markings (called “belton” pattern), along with long pendant ears set low, a gentle.
german shorthaired: a German Shorthaired Pointer is identified by its sleek, muscular build, short dense coat typically in liver or liver-and-white patterns, distinctive floppy ears set high on the head, and a tightly curled or saber-like tail often docked to medium length.
great pyrenees: a great pyrenees is identified by its large, muscular build, predominantly white double coat with possible light tan or grey markings on the head and ears, and distinctive facial mask or “badger” markings around the eyes.
havanese: a havanese is identified by its long, silky, wavy to curly coat that often parts naturally down the back, large expressive dark eyes with prominent eyebrows, a compact square build, and a plumed tail carried gracefully over the back.
japanese chin: a Japanese Chin is identified by a compact, square-proportioned body, a distinctly flat face with large, wide-set, dark eyes, prominent feathered ears with long, silky hair, and a high-set, plumed tail carried jauntily over the back.
keeshond: a keeshond is identified by its distinctive silver-gray and black “spectacles” facial markings, plush ruff of fur around the neck, curled fox-like tail carried over the back, and dense double coat with a characteristic “shaggy” texture and penciled markings.
leonberger: a leonberger is identified by its massive, muscular build, distinctive black facial mask contrasting with a lion-like tawny, sandy, or red coat, and a proud, gentle expression accentuated by dark, almond-shaped eyes and pendant ears.
Maine Coon: a Maine Coon is identified by its large, rectangular body with heavy boning, tufted ears, bushy tapering tail, long shaggy water-resistant fur with a prominent ruff around the neck, and distinct facial structure featuring high cheekbones and a square.
miniature pinscher: a miniature pinscher is identified by its sleek, compact body with a distinctive racy gait, erect ears that taper to pointed tips, a short smooth coat, and a high-set tail often docked to a stub, giving it a bold, alert, and terrier.
newfoundland: a Newfoundland is identified by its massive, stocky build, thick double coat with prominent ruff around the neck, triangular head with a broad skull and short muzzle, and distinctive facial expression marked by drooping upper lips and deep-set, gentle eyes.
Persian: a Persian is identified by its extremely flat, pushed-in face with prominent round eyes, long dense fur that often obscures the facial structure, and a short, stocky body with a broad head and small ears set low on the skull.
pomeranian: a Pomeranian is identified by its compact size, heavily plumed tail curled tightly over the back, foxy facial expression with a short muzzle and small erect ears, and a profuse double coat with a prominent ruff around the neck.
pug: a pug is identified by its deeply wrinkled, short-muzzled face, large dark protruding eyes, compact square body, and tightly curled tail.
Ragdoll: a Ragdoll is identified by its large blue eyes, pointed coloration with lighter body and darker face/ears/legs/tail, semi-long silky fur without an undercoat, and tendency to go limp when held.
Russian Blue: a Russian Blue is identified by its short, dense double coat of uniform blue-gray fur with silver-tipped guard hairs that create a shimmering, plush appearance, bright green almond-shaped eyes, and a slender, muscular body with a refined, wedge-shaped head and large, wide.
saint bernard: a saint bernard is identified by its massive, muscular build, broad head with pronounced wrinkles, short or medium-length dense coat (often white with reddish-brown or mahogany markings), and distinctive dark mask around the eyes and muzzle.
samoyed: a samoyed is identified by its pure white, dense double coat with a distinctive “smiling” facial expression formed by upturned mouth corners and dark, almond-shaped eyes set in a black or brown nose pigment.
scottish terrier: a scottish terrier is identified by its compact, sturdy build, short legs, long head with a prominent jaw and beard, erect ears, and dense, wiry black or brindle coat with distinct facial furnishings.
shiba inu: a shiba inu is identified by its compact, muscular build, distinct fox-like face with triangular upright ears, a curled-over tail, and a double coat with a crisp, straight outer layer and a soft, dense undercoat—often in red, black-and-tan.
Siamese: a Siamese is identified by a pale fawn-to-cream body with sharply contrasting dark brown to black points on the ears, face (including a distinct mask), paws, and tail, along with striking bright blue almond-shaped eyes.
Sphynx: a Sphynx is identified by its hairless, wrinkled skin, large lemon-shaped eyes, oversized bat-like ears, and prominent cheekbones with a wedge-shaped head.
staffordshire bull terrier: a staffordshire bull terrier is identified by its short, smooth coat; broad, muscular head with pronounced cheek muscles and a distinct stop; small, rose-shaped or half-pricked ears; and a stocky, compact body with a deep chest and well-defined jawline.
wheaten terrier: a wheaten terrier is identified by its soft, wavy to curly wheat-colored coat, rectangular body shape, gentle expressive eyes, and distinctive beard and mustache that blend seamlessly into the facial furnishings.
yorkshire terrier: a yorkshire terrier is identified by its compact size, long straight silky coat typically in steel-blue and tan coloration, small erect ears, and a confident, alert expression with dark, bright eyes.
